summary.one_liner: AI Legion is a Node.js framework for running LLM-powered autonomous agents that can work together on tasks, controlled through a console.
summary.what_it_does: Starts a configurable number of autonomous agents backed by OpenAI models (gpt-3.5-turbo or gpt-4) from the command line. Agents take actions through a text-based action format, such as asking for help on an action's parameters and using actions like writeFile. Messages typed into the console are sent to all running agents. Each agent keeps its state (memory, goals, notes) in a per-agent folder under .store, so runs resume on restart. The README says agents can search the web via the Google Custom Search API when configured. An optional delay can be set after each agent action.
use_cases: running multiple autonomous LLM agents on a shared task
experimenting with GPT-4 or gpt-3.5-turbo agents
web-searching LLM agents with Google Custom Search
debugging agent behavior by replaying saved state
studying how agents learn to use actions
how_to_run: Rename .env.template to .env and add OPENAI_API_KEY (plus GOOGLE_SEARCH_ENGINE_ID and GOOGLE_API_KEY for web search)
notable: Agents persist memory, goals, and notes under .store, so you can delete state or replay from a point in memory
Console interface broadcasts typed messages to all agents at once
Multi-line parameter values use a multiline delimiter, as described in the action errors section
Optional AGENT_DELAY setting pauses after each agent action
caveats: The README warns that gpt-3.5-turbo agents can fall into endless error loops that consume tokens quickly, so agents should not be left unattended
Requires OpenAI API key and, for web search, a Google Cloud project with Custom Search API enabled
Setup is minimal in the README; no license is stated
